text:
Alex: Heads-up — p99 is spiking for model-omega in us-west-2 this morning. Symptoms point to sustained batching pressure; max_batch is hitting 1024 and queue times blow out. Anyone oncall?
Maya: I’m here. Any numbers? which clusters?
Alex: us-west-2/gpu-pool-3. Quick snapshot:
```
p99_latency_before: 420ms -> peak 780ms
avg_batch_size: 900
max_batch_config: 1024
queue_depth: 350 -> 1200 during spikes
admission_reject_rate: 0.8% (routes throttled)
GPU_util: 92-96% sustained
```
Rick: That pattern screams head-of-line when a few giant batches run long. Admission controller only rejects at 95% occupancy so many requests queue behind huge batches.
Jen: Rolled a canary patch — temporarily lowered max_batch to 512 on a subset of nodes. Early signal: p99 down to ~330ms, queue depth capped ~420.
Sofia: Good quick mitigation. We should avoid manual fiddles as long-term fix. Proposal: make max_batch adaptive per-model and per-shard based on observed service_time distribution + target occupancy (target 75-80%).
Chris: FWIW smaller batches increase per-token GPU overhead. Our rough calc: moving from 1024->512 increased GPU cost ~12% for dense workloads. Need to weigh SLO delta vs cost.
Maya: Also note region constraints — us-west-2 only has V100s in that fleet. us-east-1 has spare A100 headroom but routing currently prefers regional affinity for latency.
Alex: Can we do a quick traffic shift for the most impacted routes to us-east-1 while we implement adaptive batching?
deploy-bot: autoscaler: initiating conservative reroute: shift 10% model-omega traffic -> us-east-1 (canary). monitoring for 15m.
Jen: Command used to adjust admission policy (canary):
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal/redwood/admission -d '{"model":"model-omega","policy":"canary","max_batch":512,"target_occupancy":0.78}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}"
```
Rick: Long term ideas:
- Admission controller should be batch-size-aware (prefer small/medium batches when queue_depth > threshold)
- Add fractional batching: allow splitting queued requests into sub-batches preemptively when a running batch exceeds latency guardrail
- Expose per-route QoS tokens so critical routes get priority capacity not whole-batch starvation
Sofia: Agree. Prioritize: 1) adaptive max_batch rollout, 2) batch-aware admission policy, 3) routing fallback to spare regions for SLO-critical tenants. Engineer estimate: 2-3 sprints for full rollout.
Chris: Add cost analysis to the RFC — include token-unit delta for expected traffic. Ops: add an alert for sustained GPU_util >90%+p99>400ms so we don’t hit this blind.
Alex: For immediate action: keep canary (512) + 10% traffic shift. I'll own the runbook updates and rollback thresholds. Jen, can you confirm telemetry dashboard widgets (p99, avg_batch, queue_depth, reject_rate) reflect both regions?
Jen: On it. I’ll push dashboard changes and add the alert.
Sofia: Assign owners and timeline in #eng-runtime planning doc. Good catch, Alex.
Alex: thanks all — will post follow-up with initial 30m canary metrics.
